candidate_relations.reason: The child has selective lower-lip asymmetry with preserved forehead, eye closure, nasolabial folds, and resting symmetry, not facial hemiparesis.

candidate_relations.reason: The reproducible congenital asymmetric crying facies is attributable to unilateral depressor anguli oris hypoplasia, not merely a normal variant.

candidate_relations.reason: Normal neurodevelopment and selective lower-lip asymmetry without other upper motor neuron findings do not support central facial palsy.
